name: Liz Truss and Kwasi Kwarteng

summary.text: Liz Truss was UK Prime Minister and Kwasi Kwarteng Chancellor of the Exchequer when the 'mini-budget' of Friday 23 September 2022 was followed by a sharp rise in gilt yields and forced selling by liability-driven investment (LDI) pension funds. The Bank of England announced a temporary backstop gilt purchase facility on 28 September 2022 with a ceiling of £65 billion, bought £19.3 billion of gilts by 14 October, and fully unwound the portfolio by 12 January 2023.

sources.title: Letter from the Chancellor of the Exchequer to the Governor of the Bank of England, 16 January 2023
Financial stability buy/sell tools: a gilt market case study (Quarterly Bulletin 2023)
Putting Out the NBFIRE: Lessons from the UK's Liability-Driven Investment (LDI) Crisis (WP/23/210)

facts.claim: The 'mini-budget' was delivered on Friday 23 September 2022; in the following days distressed forced selling of gilts by LDI funds produced fire-sale dynamics in the UK government bond market.
facts.quote: distressed forced selling of gilts by liability-driven investment (LDI) funds led to fire-sale dynamics

sources.title: Putting Out the NBFIRE: Lessons from the UK's Liability-Driven Investment (LDI) Crisis (WP/23/210)

sources.publisher: Stewarts (law firm note on the House of Lords Industry and Regulators Committee)
sources.title: House of Lords committee outlines recommendations for improving regulation of LDI

facts.claim: The Bank of England announced its temporary and targeted gilt purchase intervention on 28 September 2022 following a recommendation from the Financial Policy Committee, with a programme ceiling of up to £65 billion; the daily limit was raised from £5 billion to £10 billion on 10 October and purchases ceased on 14 October 2022.

sources.title: Financial stability buy/sell tools: a gilt market case study (Quarterly Bulletin 2023)
Bank of England doubles bond buying daily limit to £10 billion

facts.claim: The Chancellor's letter of 16 January 2023 records that the Bank purchased a £19.3 billion gilt portfolio between 28 September and 14 October 2022, announced on 10 November 2022 its intention to unwind it, and completed the unwind on 12 January 2023.
facts.quote: unwind the £19.3 billion gilt portfolio purchased in the temporary and targeted financial stability intervention, conducted between 28 September and 14 October 2022

sources.title: Letter from the Chancellor of the Exchequer to the Governor of the Bank of England, 16 January 2023

facts.claim: The House of Lords Industry and Regulators Committee wrote to the government on 7 February 2023 concluding that the Bank of England, the FCA and The Pensions Regulator had all failed to focus sufficiently on the risks of LDI strategies; its chair Lord Hollick said the regulators 'were all blindsided'.
facts.quote: the Bank, the City watchdog and The Pensions Regulator (TPR) all failed to sufficiently focus on the risks associated with LDI strategies

sources.publisher: Stewarts (law firm note on the House of Lords Industry and Regulators Committee)
sources.title: House of Lords committee outlines recommendations for improving regulation of LDI

facts.claim: Truss has said that neither she nor Kwarteng had been informed about the pensions 'tinderbox' before the mini-budget.
facts.quote: neither she nor her chancellor, Kwasi Kwarteng, had been informed about the pensions "tinderbox" before the mini-Budget

sources.title: Report on Truss remarks about LDI 'tinderbox'

connections.claim: The Bank of England's £19.3 billion gilt purchase intervention of 28 September-14 October 2022 followed the Truss-Kwarteng mini-budget.

sources.title: Letter from the Chancellor of the Exchequer to the Governor of the Bank of England, 16 January 2023

connections.claim: Bailey, as Governor, was the addressee of the Chancellor's January 2023 letter closing the gilt intervention that followed the mini-budget.

sources.title: Letter from the Chancellor of the Exchequer to the Governor of the Bank of England, 16 January 2023

openQuestions: Site claim tested: the £65 billion ceiling, the 28 September-14 October window and the roughly £19 billion of purchases are supported (exact figure £19.3 billion). The page's '100 basis points in days' yield move was not tested here. The site lists Truss and Kwarteng as one entity; this file follows that id.
